program_question: Do restricted correspondences between adaptive dynamical systems support quantitative stability laws and no-refit cross-class transport, or only local coordinate equivalences?

map.state: interior categorical probability vector p on the simplex
map.geometry: negative-entropy mirror geometry = categorical Fisher/Shahshahani geometry
map.clean_update: p_i' proportional to p_i exp(eta r_i)

scope: strictly interior clean states for KL/Fisher expressions
exact exponential categorical update or its stated continuous-time limit
float64 numerical comparisons at declared horizons and tolerances
edges.content: Within scope, the mapped clean probability trajectories must agree; ACL-002 additionally predicts the first-order L1 response to a frozen row-stochastic mutation perturbation.

stability.result: ACL-002 zero-fit analytic target gate passed. Posthoc residuals are predominantly negative, locally quadratic for T>1, and landscape dependent.

second_order_exploratory.result: The frozen posthoc earning rule passed with no target refit; all 12 regular T=20 targets gained 5% and 10% radius, but stress stability failed.

second_order_confirmation.law: delta_L1^(2)(epsilon,T) = ||epsilon s_T + (epsilon^2/2) u_T||_1 with O(epsilon^3) state remainder
second_order_confirmation.result: ACL-003 passed on 16 landscapes using entirely new state, reward, and mutation catalog values. At T=20, the maximum relative error per landscape over epsilon 0.001, 0.003, and 0.01 had median 0.148431% and Type-7 Q90 0.738712% with no fitting.

transport.quantity: median source-landscape alpha multiplying the analytic first-order coefficient
transport.result: Passed on 12 deterministic held-out target combinations with frozen alpha_source = 0.9951356698171323.
transport.scope_limit: within-family combinatorial held-out transport, not a different adaptive-system class

second_order_new_value.quantity: zero-fit analytic second-order truncated state response
second_order_new_value.result: Passed on 16 new-value categorical landscapes through epsilon 0.01.
second_order_new_value.scope_limit: stronger new-value transport within the categorical mutation class, not cross-class transport

failure_boundary.result: ACL-003 confirms second-order accuracy through epsilon 0.01 on new values. Stored non-gating stress rows show improvement on all 16 landscapes at epsilon 0.03 but only 13 at epsilon 0.1; T=20 second-order stress median is 3.652%, Q90 36.875%, and maximum 114.694%. The law is not uniformly stress-stable.
failure_boundary.unresolved: The exact analytic radius sufficient for uniform error control remains open; no cross-class stability transport has yet been tested.

edges.what_would_change_interpretation: Failure of an independently defined Gaussian bridge would confine the present predictive law to the categorical class; successful no-refit cross-class transport would support a restricted reusable correspondence theory.

map.candidate_update: separate mean and covariance rank-mu tangent blocks

scope: frozen lambda, mu, weights, parameterization, and learning rates
edges.content: The conditional expected finite-lambda rank-mu update should align with an independently constructed analytic Fisher-natural direction in each tangent block.
edges.what_would_change_interpretation: A preregistered conditional-mean Fisher cosine failure after shadow convergence would reject the proposed Gaussian bridge under its frozen finite-lambda scope.

edges.content: A control-class bridge would require a preregistered quantity from an earlier class to predict a held-out policy response without control-target refitting.
edges.what_would_change_interpretation: If no source-class law can be stated before observing control outcomes, this edge remains a coordinate relationship rather than evidence of reusable transport.
